h1: The Zen Hotel Yasothon — a boutique hotel with private balconies in the city centre, near Ban Singha Tha
intro: In a town where most hotels lean plain, The Zen Hotel positions itself as a small 30-room boutique hotel on Wari Ratchadech Road with a calm, true-to-its-name feel · The standout guests mention most is that every room has a private balcony, the beds are firm and comfy, rooms are clean, the A/C cold, with free bottled water, free Wi-Fi and free parking, plus a 24-hour front desk · It's central, a short hop to the Ban Singha Tha old town, with eateries and street food all around · From approx. ฿650/night · Real guest reviews praise clean rooms, good beds, friendly staff and good value · It scores 8.9 from 47 reviews on Trip.com — high for a hotel in a secondary town.

body.html: The Zen Hotel is a 30-room boutique hotel in central Yasothon, on Wari Ratchadech Road in the Nai Mueang subdistrict · The hotel is built around a calm concept that lives up to the Zen name, with rooms and common areas in restful, understated tones · Its signature is that every room has a private balcony — somewhere to step out for the breeze or a morning coffee, which is rare in a few-hundred-baht hotel in a secondary town · Rooms come with twin or queen beds, suiting solo travellers, couples and business visitors alike.

What guests consistently praise is that the rooms are clean, the beds firm and comfy, the A/C cold and the rooms look neat and newish · Every room has a flat-screen TV, complimentary water, an en-suite bathroom and Wi-Fi · Many reviews say they slept well thanks to the firm-but-comfy beds and the quiet rooms · The hotel runs a 24-hour front desk, with free parking and laundry service, handy for self-drivers or anyone arriving in Yasothon late · There's an in-house Zen Cafe for a coffee, even though breakfast isn't included with the room · Its compact size means staff are attentive and friendly.
"Clean room, very comfortable bed, cold A/C, and even a private balcony · friendly staff, free parking, central and walkable to Ban Singha Tha — great value at this price."

Location is another advantage · The hotel is central in Yasothon on Wari Ratchadech Road, near the Ban Singha Tha old town — the row of old wooden shophouses that's the town's signature spot — and close to Wat Maha That, the Yasothon city museum and the town market · Eateries, cafés and street food surround the hotel, so food is easy to find day and night · It suits old-town visitors, official-business travellers, or anyone stopping over for a night on an Isan trip · Phaya Thaen Park and the city's green spaces are a short drive away.

To be straight with you, per real guest reviews: the limitations that come up are that staff speak limited English, so international travellers may need a translation app · Some reviews note the Wi-Fi signal can be weak at times, and a few rooms have low water pressure · Breakfast isn't included with the room and the in-house café opens late (around 10:30), so an early breakfast means heading out · It's a small, rooms-only hotel — no pool or gym like a bigger property.

In short: if you want accommodation in central Yasothon that's clean, with good beds, a private balcony, free parking and a central location near Ban Singha Tha, at a few hundred baht — The Zen Hotel is a fitting choice, calmer than the hotels on the main road · It scores 8.9 from 47 reviews on Trip.com, clearly positive · It suits couples, solo travellers and business visitors who value cleanliness and value over a full set of facilities.

A tip from following the reviews here: ask for a room whose balcony faces a quieter side, so you can enjoy the morning breeze in peace · If you're travelling with non-Thai speakers, keep a translation app handy, as staff speak limited English · There's no included breakfast, so plan to grab street food around Ban Singha Tha in the morning · And with a 24-hour front desk, a late arrival is no problem — you can check in any time.

faq.q: Where is The Zen Hotel in Yasothon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The Zen Hotel is at 245 Wari Ratchadech Road, Nai Mueang subdistrict, in central Yasothon · It's about a 3-5 minute drive from the Ban Singha Tha old town, Wat Maha That, the Yasothon city museum and the town market · Eateries, cafés and street food surround the hotel, so food is easy to find day and night.

faq.q: How much does The Zen Hotel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿650/night for a Standard Twin or Standard Queen · Superior and Deluxe rooms run about ฿790-฿950 · Prices vary by room type and season, so compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does every room at The Zen Hotel really have a balcony?
faq.a: Yes, every room has a private balcony · It's the standout guests mention most — somewhere to step out for the breeze or a morning coffee · Every room also has A/C, a flat-screen TV, complimentary water, an en-suite bathroom and free Wi-Fi.

faq.q: Who is The Zen Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for couples, solo travellers and business visitors who want clean accommodation with good beds, a private balcony and a central location near Ban Singha Tha, at a few hundred baht · It suits old-town visitors, official-business travellers and anyone stopping over for a night on an Isan trip, favouring cleanliness and value over a full set of facilities.

faq.q: Does The Zen Hotel serve breakfast?
faq.a: No breakfast is included with the room · There's an in-house Zen Cafe for a coffee, but it opens fairly late (around 10:30) · For an early breakfast, head out to the street food and rice-porridge spots around Ban Singha Tha and the town market.

faq.q: Does The Zen Hotel have parking and late check-in?
faq.a: Yes — free parking and a 24-hour front desk with round-the-clock check-in, handy for self-drivers or anyone arriving in Yasothon late · Laundry service is available too · It's a small, rooms-only hotel with no pool or gym.
